decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right, pens on the left. Begin turning right gripper inward with gradual elbow-up motion; left stays home.
Move right hand around the outside of the holder and finish inward-facing orientation, keeping fingers open.
Prior chunk rejected without motion. Reduce translation and rotation increments to preserve joint continuity during the outside approach.
Replan after wrist continuity interruption: approach holder from the front rather than its far outside, unwinding yaw gradually.
Align the open right jaws forward around the holder, lowering slowly. Watch for cup displacement before closing.
Holder tipped during alignment. Close around its near end and make a small test lift before attempting to right it.
Test lift showed no retention. Open and move above the fallen holder, pitching the gripper downward for a body grasp.
Continue the overhead approach to the fallen holder, keeping jaws open and motion gradual.
Close around the holder body and test a vertical lift. Verify retention from the next images before rotating it upright.
Holder appears retained. Lift and rotate its far opening upward while bringing it toward the middle of the right workspace.
Finish righting the held holder with a slow rotation, and bring it closer to the center without crossing arms.
Turn the held cup toward the center and lower it slightly, while beginning the left arm's overhead pen approach.
Cup is upright and retained. Finish positioning its opening near center; approach the purple pen from above with the left hand.
Lower the left jaws around the purple pen near its capped end. Hold the cup steady with the right hand.
Close the left jaws at the purple pen and test retention with a short vertical lift; avoid further table contact.
Purple pen is visibly retained. Lift clear of the table and rotate it toward vertical while keeping the cup steady.
Turn the vertical purple pen inward toward the cup, maintaining clearance above its rim.
Align the purple pen over the cup opening, with a small upward clearance before insertion.
Lower the purple pen slowly through the visible opening while retaining both objects.
Release the purple pen into the holder, then withdraw the left gripper upward and left without disturbing the cup.
Purple pen remains in the cup. Reorient the left hand for an overhead grasp of the cyan pen, keeping above the objects.
Complete the downward orientation and move above the cyan pen's capped half, retaining clearance.
After the continuity rejection, lower without extending farther and use smaller rotational increments to complete the overhead grasp orientation.
Move the open left jaws onto the cyan pen's capped half with a slow downward approach; right hand remains steady.
Replan after IK rejection: use a slightly forward-angled grasp to reduce elbow folding, lowering while retracting the wrist.
Previous action moved neither arm. Use much smaller angular and positional increments to leave the near-limit posture continuously.
Continue the angled descent toward the cyan pen, keeping the wrist clear and preserving the recovered elbow configuration.
Close on the cyan pen, then test a small upward lift before transporting it.
Cyan pen is visibly retained. Lift and retract it while beginning to turn it upright, clear of the other pens.
Turn the retained cyan pen inward and upright above the holder's rim, maintaining clearance.
Align cyan pen over the open space beside the purple pen, descending cautiously toward the rim.
Guide the cyan pen a little deeper into the opening, slightly left of the rim, before releasing it.
Release the cyan pen inside the cup, then withdraw up and left to inspect retention.
Both colored pens remain in the cup. Retract and turn the left hand toward the nearer white pen.
Approach the nearer white pen from above, pitching downward and keeping its capped end between the open jaws.
Lower around the white pen's upper body, correcting slightly toward the robot to center the grasp.
Center the narrow white pen between the jaws, close, and make a small test lift.
The white pen is retained. Lift it clear and rotate its long axis upright before moving over the holder.
Turn the upright white pen inward and bring it above the remaining space in the cup.
Lower the white pen toward the open space behind the colored pens, maintaining a closed grasp.
Seat the white pen slightly deeper and release it into the holder beside the colored pens.
The first white pen is in the cup. Withdraw left and align the gripper's heading with the last diagonal white pen.
Approach the last white pen from above while pitching the gripper downward along its diagonal axis.
Complete the overhead orientation and descend toward the last white pen's upper body, keeping jaws open.
Correct the lateral offset visible in the left wrist view and lower the open jaws around the last white pen.
Finish centering on the last white pen, close the jaws, and test a short lift.
Last white pen is visibly retained. Retract and lift while gradually turning it upright, keeping the elbow configuration continuous.
Rejected chunk executed no motion. Use smaller increments to retract from the extended pickup posture while retaining the pen.
Continue lifting and retracting the last pen while turning it vertical, now clear of the extended posture.
Turn the vertical final pen inward and align above the holder, keeping it clear of the three inserted pens.
Lower the final white pen into the remaining gap in the holder, with a small leftward alignment correction.
Release the final pen into the cup, then withdraw the left hand upward and left to check all four remain inside.
All four pens are visible in the holder. Begin lowering and straightening the filled cup while retracting the left arm toward home.
Replan from the interrupted pose. Keep the now-upright cup orientation and lower slowly toward the table while the left arm returns near home.
The filled cup appears supported upright on the table. Open the right hand and withdraw gently; complete the left hand's return to origin.
The cup leaned during withdrawal. Clear the open right jaws upward and back, unwinding the wrist away from its limit; inspect whether the cup settles upright.
No motion on rejection. Bridge the wrist tracking residual first, then slowly retract with open jaws while unwinding yaw.
